2. (New) An electronic device for long-term adhesion to a mammal, the device comprising:
a housing comprising a physiologic data collection circuit, the housing positioned over a flexible layer extending from beneath the housing and comprising an electrode positioned on an underside of the flexible layer distal from the housing, wherein the flexible layer comprises:
a substrate upper layer overlying an electrical connection, the electrical connection extending linearly from the data collection circuit to the electrode when viewed from above the electronic device,
an upper adhesive layer positioned under the substrate upper layer, the upper adhesive layer adhering the substrate upper layer to a substrate lower layer underlying the electrical connection, and a lower adhesive layer positioned on the underside of the flexible layer and extending from beneath the housing to the electrode, the lower adhesive layer configured to provide adhesion to the skin of the mammal.
3. (New) The electronic device of claim 2, wherein the lower adhesive layer extends at least partially below the housing.
4. (New) The electronic device of claim 2, further comprising a flap extending beneath the housing.
5. (New) The electronic device of claim 2, wherein the housing is rigid.
6. (New) The electronic device of claim 2, wherein the housing is configured to remain connected to the flexible layer when the housing is tilted at an angle relative the adhesive layer in response to movement of the user.
7. (New) The electronic device of claim 2, further comprising a hinge portion adjacent the housing.
8. (New) The electronic device of claim 2, wherein the adhesive layer comprises a hydrocolloid adhesive.
9. (New) The electronic device of claim 2, wherein the physiologic data collection circuit is configured to collect cardiac rhythm data from the user.
10. (New) An electronic device for long-term adhesion to a mammal, the device comprising:
a housing comprising a physiologic data collection circuit;
an electrode-supporting section comprising a first substrate layer, a second substrate layer, and a lower adhesive layer positioned on a bottom surface, the lower adhesive layer providing adhesion to the skin of the mammal;
an electrode positioned on the bottom surface of the electrode-supporting section, the electrode electrically connected to the physiologic data collection circuit; and
a first substrate layer positioned over the electrode and extending horizontally away from the housing beyond a boundary of the electrode; and
a second substrate layer positioned over the first substrate layer and extending horizontally away from the housing beyond the boundary of the first substrate layer.
11. (New) The electronic device of claim 10, wherein the electrode supporting section further comprises a third substrate layer adhered to the first substrate layer.
12. (New) The electronic device of claim 10, further comprising an upper adhesive layer positioned on the underside of the first substrate layer.
13. (New) The electronic device of claim 10, wherein the lower adhesive layer extends at least partially below the housing.
14. (New) The electronic device of claim 10, further comprising a flap extending beneath the housing.
15. (New) The electronic device of claim 10, wherein the housing is rigid.
16. (New) The electronic device of claim 10, wherein the housing is configured to remain connected to the electrode-supporting section when the housing is tilted at an angle relative the lower adhesive layer in response to movement of the user.
17. (New) The electronic device of claim 10, further comprising a hinge portion adjacent the housing.
18. (New) The electronic device of claim 10, wherein the lower adhesive layer comprises a hydrocolloid adhesive.
19. (New) The electronic device of claim 10, wherein the physiologic data collection circuit is configured to collect cardiac rhythm data from the user.
